note: Jason's life, written by hand to go with the film. Up to late 2026 it follows what the owner said; 'invented' people and everything after 2026 are made up. Years are decimals (2022.75 is early October). 'curve' is closeness over time, 0 to 1: 0.18 friend, 0.4 close, 0.62 inner circle.

people.name: Mom
beats: Your mom runs Orient Buffet in Cumberland with your dad. You grew up in it.
You move back home after graduating. She does not mind.
She packs enough food for a week for a four-hour drive.

people.name: Dad
beats: Your dad runs Orient Buffet in Cumberland with your mom.
He checks the tyres twice before you leave for New York.

people.name: James Chen
beats: James is your brother.
You are both back in Cumberland for a while.

people.name: Jeffrey Chen
beats: Jeffrey is your brother.

people.name: Auntie Lin
beats: Your mom's side of the family is in New York.
When you move to New York she is twenty minutes away, and you eat there every Sunday.

people.name: Kevin Lin
beats: Kevin is your cousin in New York.
He finds you the apartment. It is two blocks from courts and two blocks from a Chipotle.

people.name: Eric Chen
people.label: met over a pair of shoes
beats: The morning after a camping trip, someone drives off in your blue shoes. He comes back half an hour later wearing them. You are wearing his.
A few weeks into algorithms he sits down next to you in Iribe. He has been playing chess the whole class.
He makes you run to the Xfinity Center in the pouring rain, so that you will remember it.
He moves to San Francisco with Calvin.
You sleep on his couch for three weeks.
The night before he flies out, he tells you this is the good part.
You move to San Francisco. He lives ten minutes away, uphill.

people.name: Momo Shaikh
people.label: met through the camping trip
people.trait: tells you what is going on
beats: Momo is driving the car that brings your shoes back.
Barbecue nights at your place: you, Eric and Momo split three hundred dollars at H Mart.
He does not want pho. You went on Tuesday.

people.name: Calvin Shi
people.label: from volleyball
beats: You play volleyball with Calvin.
You bring him to Eric's birthday. Fifteen months later the two of them share an apartment in San Francisco.
He keeps count of how many days you have left to find a date.

people.label: from College Park

beats: You know Berek from College Park.
In San Francisco he gets you a two-month gym trial and plays doubles with you.
You turn twenty-four at his house.

people.name: Emily Nguyen
people.label: through Eric
beats: Emily comes to the barbecue nights.
Outside your place, in the cold, Eric asks her. You had forgotten he was doing that today.

people.name: Daniel Wei
people.label: came to barbecue
beats: Ten people came to barbecue. One of them was Daniel.
Dinner in San Francisco a few days before your birthday. You pick pho.

people.name: Jocelyn Choo
people.label: from College Park
beats: You know Jocelyn from College Park.
She moves to New York.
When you move to New York she is the one person there you already know who is not family.

people.name: David
people.label: from San Francisco
beats: David makes you a whole birthday cake. Then he buys another one, too.

people.name: Tomoka

beats: You go back into the bar to talk to her. You ask her for a referral. You email twice.

people.name: Linh Pham

beats: One of the VSA littles who comes to barbecue.

people.name: Kevin Tran

beats: He booked the campsite.

people.name: Marcus Lee

beats: Volleyball, with Calvin.

people.name: Priya Patel

people.name: Anna Kim

people.name: Sam Ortiz
people.label: met on a court
beats: You say, "I see you like tennis." He is holding a racket, on a tennis court. You play twice a week for five years.

people.name: Mei Lin

beats: You walk up to her and say, "I see you like tennis." She is on a tennis court, holding a racket.
It worked.
You move to San Francisco together.

threads: Eric took your shoes. Through him came Momo, who was driving, and Emily.
You brought Calvin to Eric's birthday. They ended up sharing an apartment in San Francisco, which is why you had a couch to sleep on.
Berek got you into the gym, and it was at his house that David brought the cake.
moments: You start at Maryland, in College Park, two and a half hours from Cumberland.
The morning after a camping trip, Eric Chen drives off in your blue shoes. He comes back half an hour later. "Seems like you took my shoes." His are pretty comfortable.
A few weeks into algorithms, the shoe guy sits down next to you in Iribe. You spend the rest of the semester next to each other.
Barbecue at your place. You, Eric and Momo split three hundred and twelve dollars at H Mart: thirty Chipotle bowls. Ten people came. One of them was Daniel Wei.
Outside your place, late and cold, Eric asks Emily. She says yes. At your place, though. That's kind of nice.
It is pouring. Eric says you will remember it when you are forty. You run to the Xfinity Center. Then Pho 75.
You bring Calvin to Eric's birthday. He was told there would be drinks.
You graduate at twenty-one and move back home to Cumberland. You say you are old.
You start at Booz Allen, from your bedroom. Laptop open at nine, closed at five, games till two.
Eric and Calvin move to San Francisco.
You fly to San Francisco and sleep on the couch for three weeks. It was free. The hills are crazy.
Berek gets you a free trial at the gym on Castro Street. Everyone in there is huge. You are small, man.
A month in San Francisco. Forty minutes waiting for a court at Mission Dolores, most days. You tell a stranger you see he likes tennis.
Both of you looking for work at the Capital One Café. Eric is on his third round. You pick Chipotle.
You go back into the bar to talk to Tomoka, and ask her for a referral for Apple. You email twice.
The night before Eric flies out. He says you cannot tell the good times while you are still in them. It is the rain thing.
You turn twenty-four at Berek's house. David makes a cake and buys another. You lost the bet: there is a video, and there are hip thrusts.
You take the job and leave Cumberland for New York. Mom packs food for a week. Eric drives out to see you off.
Jocelyn shows you which train is which.
"I see you like tennis." Sam Ortiz is holding a racket, on a tennis court.
"I see you like tennis." Mei Lin is on a tennis court, holding a racket. It works.
You and Mei are together. Eric tells you to enjoy your money while you still have it.
You and Mei move to San Francisco. There are courts two blocks away. Everything is uphill.
Tennis with Eric and Calvin again, at Mission Dolores. You take a phone call and walk off down the baseline.
You turn forty. You remember the run in the rain.
A bench at Mission Dolores, waiting for a court. You look at Eric's shoes.
story: You're 18. At the table: your mom, your dad, and your brothers James and Jeffrey.
Someone has driven off in your blue shoes. He comes back wearing them. You are wearing his. That is Eric.
He sits down next to you in algorithms. Neither of you gets any of it.
He makes you run in the pouring rain, so that you will remember it.
Eric moves to San Francisco. You are in Cumberland, at home, saying you are old. You are twenty-two.
You fly out and sleep on the couch for three weeks.
The night before he flies out, he tells you this is the good part.
You take the job and leave home.
"I see you like tennis." It worked.
You and Mei move to San Francisco. Eric is ten minutes away, uphill.
Without one pair of blue shoes: no Eric, and so no Momo and no Emily.
You said you were old at twenty-one. You are fifty-eight. It was all the good part.
